A Ground-First Machine

There's no bell-cow to bank on — the lead back sees just 50% of carries (league ~59%), a committee that caps any one back's ceiling and makes their rushing props matchup- and script-dependent.

The Offensive Blueprint

NE throw by design. They pass -0% over expectation (league -2%) and keep firing even with a lead (39% early-down pass when ahead vs ~41%) — the kind of pass-first identity that keeps receivers live in every script.

The tight end is a genuine centerpiece, not an afterthought — 18% of targets (league ~15%).

Their quarterback is a scramble threat — he takes off on 5.8% of dropbacks (nearly double the 3.3% norm), rushing production that both lifts his own yardage and siphons a few carries from the backfield.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they lean run-heavy, passing 51% of the time, funnelling touchdown equity to the lead back. And with the TE commanding 18% of targets, the tight end is a live red-zone option too.

Defense — A Balanced Defense

They lock down opposing WR1s — just 50 rec yds/game (vs ~58); fade receiving props there.

They surrender 114 rushing and 210 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). No dominant funnel — read it matchup by matchup.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
